title: Articles XXXII–XXXVII · On further aspects of the first species: the Trinity's perfections, the processions, and practice of this contemplation

blocks.s: [Articles XXXII–XXXVII continue the development of the first species of contemplation of the most holy Trinity, treating the eternal processions of Son and Holy Spirit, the attributes of each Person, the mutual indwelling of the Persons, and the practical manner in which the contemplative soul is to raise itself to this most divine of all contemplations. Denis draws throughout on Dionysius, Augustine, Bonaventure, Aquinas and the tradition of the mystical theologians, and exhorts the contemplator to combine the most exact doctrinal faith with the deepest humility and the most ardent charity, approaching this contemplation always with purified intellect, composed and collected mind, and heart wholly set on God; and to bring the contemplation to its conclusion in praise, thanksgiving, and the most ardent self-surrender to the most Holy Trinity.]
